summary: Built on Brundage Mountain near McCall from 1914 onward; the 1982 cab is still staffed in fire season, but its tower is not open to the public.

facts.design: Two-story flat-top cab; the register says concrete and wood on a rubble base

access.note: Viewing platform open to the public; the tower itself is not open because it is an active residence and workplace.

visit.trail_note: Reached from the top of the Bluebird Express chairlift; the Lookout Trail is rocky but relatively flat along the summit ridge.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1914 is the first log cabin and platform tower, 1919 the first two-story log house, and 1982 the current cab. The record's 1982 matches the current cab; firelookout.com's 1919 describes an earlier house on the same site.

notes_for_editor: Disputed: the 20x20 log lookout is dated 1929 by the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts but to the 1930s by Forest Lookouts. The 1982 cab is described three ways (concrete and wood on rubble base; wooden on concrete slab; cinder block and wood frame). Administration is unresolved: the register says the timber association administers it, while the resort calls it an active Forest Service lookout. Elevation is 7,569 ft in the register and 7,552 ft on two sites. The register says Valley County; firelookout.com says Valley/Adams. The 2025 staffing as_of comes from the Idaho Fire Lookouts page dated March 26, 2025. The tower record's built=1919 (firelookout_com) describes the earlier house, not the current cab. Leads not read and not cited: a University of Idaho 1990 report on Payette NF fire control history, and a 1933 Idaho Statesman item in the McCall Public Library collection. Recommend checking current staffing and public access with SITPA or the Payette NF before publishing.
